en.title: New Doc 'American Doctor' Drops on Streaming, Offering Harrowing Gaza Insights
en.summary: A powerful new documentary, 'American Doctor,' has just landed on streaming platforms, shining a light on the courageous medical professionals working in Gaza. The film presents a stark look at the ongoing conflict through the eyes of those on the front lines.
en.body:
This week, the streaming landscape welcomes a documentary that demands your attention: **American Doctor**. Directed by **Poh Si Teng**, the film arrives on Prime Video, offering a harrowing and deeply moving portrait of the doctors risking their lives in the Gaza Strip. It’s a difficult watch, but an essential one, particularly in its unflinching gaze at the overwhelming victims of the ongoing genocide.

**American Doctor** focuses on three remarkable individuals: Dr. Feroze Sidhwa, Dr. Thaer Ahmad, and Dr. Mark Perlmutter. These physicians, hailing from diverse backgrounds—Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—are united by their commitment to saving lives amidst an escalating crisis. The documentary captures the arduous reality of their work, detailing how access to Gaza is often a gamble, with approvals granted on some trips and denied for opaque reasons on others. It's a stark reminder of the geopolitical complexities and the human cost that define this conflict. As noted in a Sundance review by Dan Mecca, the film asks critical questions: “When will this end? When will this bloodshed stop? And when will the United States of America stop supporting it?” **Poh Si Teng** provides a clear-eyed, unrelenting look at the genocide in Gaza through the dedication of these doctors.

## A Glimpse into the Heart of the Crisis

The film doesn't shy away from the devastating impact of the conflict on the ground. We witness the immense pressure these doctors face, not only the physical toll of treating an overwhelming number of casualties but also the emotional burden of working in such extreme conditions. Their dedication is a testament to the enduring spirit of humanity, even when faced with immense suffering and systemic obstacles. The narrative weaves together personal stories with the broader political context, making it a powerful call for awareness and empathy. It’s a vital piece of cinema for anyone seeking to understand the realities beyond the headlines.

## What This Means for Viewers

For fans of impactful documentaries and those passionate about global affairs, **American Doctor** is a must-see. It provides a platform for voices that are often unheard and sheds light on a situation that continues to affect countless lives. The film’s arrival on streaming makes it accessible to a global audience, fostering a deeper understanding and encouraging important conversations. In a world saturated with content, this documentary stands out for its urgency and its profound humanistic message. It’s a powerful reminder of the courage found in the most challenging circumstances and the importance of bearing witness.

## What's Next

**American Doctor** is now available to stream on Prime Video in the United States. Viewers can expect a raw and deeply affecting cinematic experience that offers a critical perspective on a complex global issue.

content_raw: Each week we highlight the noteworthy titles that have recently hit streaming platforms in the United States. Check out this week’s selections below and past round-ups  here . Ali G: Who Iz I? (Sacha Baron Cohen) After a perfunctory, slimmed-down theatrical release last weekend, Sacha Baron Cohen’s feature directorial debut has now arrived on Prime Video. Anyone familiar with the comedian’s hijinks, and particularly Borat 2 and Who Is America? , will know what to expect when it comes to this Ali G sequel: a clunky and strained (albeit sporadically funny) reckoning with modern political and societal ills that feels a little too late to the game to pack a genuinely hilarious punch. As streaming slop, one could get much worse, but especially with his last few projects, it feels like Baron Cohen is seemingly content with shooting fish in a barrel. Where to Stream: Prime Video American Doctor (Poh Si Teng) Poh Si Teng’s  American Doctor  is a harrowing, heartbreaking portrait of Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian doctors who are risking their lives to tend to the overwhelming victims of the ongoing genocide in Gaza and speak the truth in any way they can. Dan Mecca said in  his Sundance review , “When will this end? When will this bloodshed stop? And when will the United States of America stop supporting it? Filmmaker Poh Si Teng offers a clear-eyed, unrelenting look at the genocide in Gaza with her documentary  American Doctor . It follows three doctors––Dr. Feroze Sidhwa, Dr. Thaer Ahmad, and Dr. Mark Perlmutter––that are consistently trying to save lives in the Gaza Strip. On some trips they are approved to enter. On others they are denied for specious reasons. Dr. Perlmutter is Jewish, Dr. Sidhwa is Zoroastrian, and Dr. Ahmad is Palestinian. Their mission is the mission of all medical professionals: to heal everyone they can.” Where to Stream: Watermelon+ (for free through November 6 only) Black Zombie (Maya Annik Bedward) More than reclaiming the zombie motif from the knee-jerk response that Night of the Living Dead inhibited, Maya Annik Bedward’s Black Zombie is a reclamation of Vodou from the colonial fear-mongering that used it to demonize Black people the world over. Because it’s 2026 and Haitians are still cautious to admit their connection to the religion. There’s still an outsider belief that Haiti’s recent hardships are a result of its ancestors making a pact with the Devil. – Jared M. He lives alongside his dog, Jasper, in an airport hangar outside of Denver.
